lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Personal Planning Systems Under Real Load
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: competing priorities and deadlines

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic competing priorities and deadlines task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner is given a fixed set of four competing obligations on this task sheet, a history project due Friday, a recurring chore commitment (trash and recycling out every Tuesday and Friday evening), a sports or club practice schedule (Monday/Wednesday/Friday 4-5:30pm), and a one-time Thursday evening family obligation (a relative's birthday dinner, 6-8pm), and must decide what to do first, second, third, and fourth this week and why.
safetyNotes: The four obligations are provided fixed scenarios on this task sheet for practice; the learner is not required to have or disclose their own real competing obligations.
materials: learner-local: this task sheet's four provided obligations

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain the general rule you used to decide what got scheduled first versus last this week (for example, fixed-time commitments first, or the obligation with the nearest deadline first), and give one real or plausible situation from your own life where that same rule would apply.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u01-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Correct handling of fixed-time conflicts: The plan correctly avoids scheduling anything into the two fixed-time blocks, placing flexible tasks only in open windows. | Quality of triage reasoning: Reasoning explicitly references the specific fixed times or the Friday deadline to justify at least one scheduling choice. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Add a fifth obligation to the scenario, a group project meeting the learner's teammate can only attend Tuesday after school, and have the learner revise their full week's plan to fit all five obligations, explaining what had to move and why.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic competing priorities and deadlines task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: competing priorities and deadlines worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner is given a fixed set of four competing obligations on this task sheet, a history project due Friday, a recurring chore commitment (trash and recycling out every Tuesday and Friday evening), a sports or club practice schedule (Monday/Wednesday/Friday 4-5:30pm), and a one-time Thursday evening family obligation (a relative's birthday dinner, 6-8pm), and must decide what to do first, second, third, and fourth this week and why.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact competing priorities and deadlines decision or action.
Model move 2: Read all four obligations below before making any decisions.
Model move 3: Identify which obligations have a hard, fixed time you cannot move and which have more flexibility.

Model check: Correct handling of fixed-time conflicts: The plan correctly avoids scheduling anything into the two fixed-time blocks, placing flexible tasks only in open windows. | Quality of triage reasoning: Reasoning explicitly references the specific fixed times or the Friday deadline to justify at least one scheduling choice.

resources.title: competing priorities and deadlines action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for competing priorities and deadlines.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: competing priorities and deadlines coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner is given a fixed set of four competing obligations on this task sheet, a history project due Friday, a recurring chore commitment (trash and recycling out every Tuesday and Friday evening), a sports or club practice schedule (Monday/Wednesday/Friday 4-5:30pm), and a one-time Thursday evening family obligation (a relative's birthday dinner, 6-8pm), and must decide what to do first, second, third, and fourth this week and why.
Coach direction: Read all four obligations below before making any decisions.
Learner prompt: For each of the four obligations, write down which day(s) it actually falls on and whether it is a fixed-time commitment or a flexible-timing one.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: competing priorities and deadlines complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Identify which obligations have a hard, fixed time you cannot move and which have more flexibility.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I identified that practice (Mon/Wed/Fri 4-5:30pm) and the birthday dinner (Thu 6-8pm) both have fixed times that cannot be moved.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I identified that the trash/recycling chore and the history project both have flexibility in exactly when during their window they get done.
Response 3 (t2-p3): Name the single obligation with the least flexibility this week and explain what makes it the least flexible.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: competing priorities and deadlines minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Explain the general rule you used to decide what got scheduled first versus last this week (for example, fixed-time commitments first, or the obligation with the nearest deadline first), and give one real or plausible situation from your own life where that same rule would apply.

Success checks: Correct handling of fixed-time conflicts: The plan correctly avoids scheduling anything into the two fixed-time blocks, placing flexible tasks only in open windows. | Quality of triage reasoning: Reasoning explicitly references the specific fixed times or the Friday deadline to justify at least one scheduling choice.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: competing priorities and deadlines supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u01-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional competing priorities and deadlines condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Correct handling of fixed-time conflicts: The plan correctly avoids scheduling anything into the two fixed-time blocks, placing flexible tasks only in open windows. | Quality of triage reasoning: Reasoning explicitly references the specific fixed times or the Friday deadline to justify at least one scheduling choice..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: competing priorities and deadlines — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the competing priorities and deadlines task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u01-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
